formulations.label: Syrup (oral calcium)
formulations.strengths: Clinic product: calcium glubionate 1.437 g + calcium lactobionate 0.295 g per 5 ml (109.3 mg calcium per 5 ml)
formulations.note: No UK product of calcium glubionate or calcium lactobionate, and no UK calcium syrup, was found on emc or MHRA Products. The UK SmPC used is for a different calcium product: an effervescent tablet of calcium lactate gluconate and calcium carbonate (1000 mg calcium per tablet, about 9 times the calcium in 5 ml of the syrup). The active (calcium) is the same, so only its calcium-class warnings, contraindications and interactions are shown. The tablet's dose, excipients and way of taking it do NOT apply to the syrup: use the clinic label for the syrup dose.

src.q: Each effervescent tablet of 1000 mg contains 2263 mg of calcium lactate gluconate and 1750 mg of calcium carbonate (equivalent to 1000 mg or 25 mmol of calcium).

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: UK calcium product: prevention and treatment of calcium deficiency; adjunct in osteoporosis; rickets and osteomalacia together with vitamin D3.

src.q: Prevention and treatment of calcium deficiency
Calcium supplement as an adjunct to specific therapy in the prevention and treatment of osteoporosis
Rickets and osteomalacia, in addition to vitamin D3 therapy

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions in the UK calcium effervescent tablet SmPC. No UK SmPC exists for the clinic's calcium glubionate/lactobionate syrup.

items.tag: UK effervescent tablet only (not the syrup)
items.t: The UK calcium effervescent tablet SmPC gives 1000 mg calcium per day for adults and children. This is the tablet's dose. There is no UK dose for the clinic syrup: use the clinic label for the syrup dose.

src.q: Adults and children: 1000mg per day.

items.tag: UK effervescent tablet only (not the syrup)
items.t: The UK calcium effervescent tablet SmPC states the same 1000 mg calcium per day for children, with no lower age limit and no weight-based dose. It does not give a dose for the syrup: use the clinic label for the syrup dose.

src.q: Adults and children: 1000mg per day.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or excipients.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 of the effervescent tablet

items.t: Diseases or conditions causing hypercalcaemia and/or hypercalciuria.

src.q: Diseases and/or conditions resulting in hypercalcaemia and/or hypercalciuria

items.t: Nephrocalcinosis, nephrolithiasis.

src.q: Nephrocalcinosis, nephrolithiasis

items.t: Mild hypercalciuria (over 300 mg or 7.5 mmol/24 hours) or history of urinary stones: monitor urinary calcium; reduce or stop if needed. Stone formers should drink more fluid.

src.q: For patients with mild hypercalciuria (exceeding 300 mg/24 hours or 7.5 mmol/24 hours), or with a history of urinary calculi, monitoring of calcium excretion in the urine is required.
An increased fluid intake is recommended for patients prone to formation of calculi in the urinary tract.

items.t: Impaired renal function: take under medical supervision with monitoring of serum calcium and phosphate.

src.q: In patients with impaired renal function, calcium salts should be taken under medical supervision with monitoring of calcium and phosphate serum levels.

items.t: High doses, especially with vitamin D: risk of hypercalcaemia and kidney impairment; monitor serum calcium and renal function.

src.q: During high dose therapy and especially during concomitant treatment with vitamin D, there is a risk of hypercalcaemia with subsequent kidney function impairment.

items.t: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion: monitor serum calcium regularly (risk of hypercalcaemia).

src.q: Due to increased risk of hypercalcaemia, serum calcium should be regularly monitored during concomitant use of thiazide diuretics.

items.t: Give tetracyclines at least 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after oral calcium.

src.q: tetracycline preparations should be administered at least two hours before or four to six hours after oral intake of calcium.

items.t: Levothyroxine SmPC: calcium salts may reduce levothyroxine absorption; separate by 4-5 hours.

src.q: Absorption of levothyroxine (thyroxine) possibly reduced by antacids, calcium salts
(administration should be separated by 4-5 hours)

items.t: Ciprofloxacin SmPC: give ciprofloxacin 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after calcium-containing products.

src.q: multivalent cation-containing drugs and mineral supplements (e.g. calcium, magnesium, aluminium, iron)
ciprofloxacin should be administered either 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after these preparations

items.t: Hypercalcaemia may increase cardiac glycoside toxicity: monitor ECG and serum calcium.

src.q: Cardiac glycoside toxicity may increase with hypercalcaemia resulting from treatment with calcium. Patients should be monitored with regard to electrocardiogram (ECG) and serum calcium levels.

items.t: Systemic corticosteroids reduce calcium absorption; the calcium dose may need to be increased.

src.q: Systemic corticosteroids reduce calcium absorption. During concomitant use, it may be necessary to increase the dose of Calvive 1000.

items.t: Oral bisphosphonates or sodium fluoride at least 3 hours before calcium. Do not take calcium within 2 hours of foods high in oxalic acid (spinach, rhubarb) or phytic acid (whole cereals).

src.q: this preparation should be administered at least three hours before the intake of Calvive 1000
The patient should not take calcium products within two hours of eating foods high in oxalic acid and phytic acid.

items.t: Impaired renal function: take calcium under medical supervision with serum calcium and phosphate monitoring (no eGFR/CrCl threshold given).

src.q: In patients with impaired renal function, calcium salts should be taken under medical supervision with monitoring of calcium and phosphate serum levels.

hepatic.note: No hepatic impairment advice in the UK calcium effervescent tablet SmPC. No UK SmPC exists for the clinic's calcium glubionate/lactobionate syrup.

items.t: Can be used in pregnancy for calcium deficiency. Adequate total intake is 1000-1300 mg calcium a day; in pregnancy total daily calcium intake should not exceed 1500 mg.

src.q: The adequate daily intake (including food and supplementation) for normal pregnant and lactating women is 1000-1300 mg calcium. During pregnancy, the daily intake of calcium should not exceed 1500 mg.

items.t: Can be used during lactation for calcium deficiency; calcium in milk causes no adverse effects in the neonate.

src.q: Significant amounts of calcium are secreted in milk during lactation but do not cause any adverse effects to the neonate.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception statements in the UK calcium effervescent tablet SmPC.

items.t: No common effects listed. Uncommon: hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria. Rare: flatulence, constipation, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain; rash, pruritus, urticaria.

src.q: Uncommon : Hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria
Rare : flatulence, constipation, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain

items.t: Very rare systemic allergic reactions (anaphylaxis, face oedema, angioneurotic oedema).

src.q: Isolated cases of systemic allergic reactions (anaphylactic reaction, face oedema, angioneurotic oedema) have been reported

items.t: Overdose: hypercalciuria and hypercalcaemia (nausea, vomiting, thirst, polyuria, dehydration, constipation). Calcium toxicity threshold: supplementation above 2000 mg a day for several months. Stop treatment and correct fluids.

src.q: The threshold for calcium intoxication is from supplementation in excess of 2000 mg per day, taken for several months.
In the case of an intoxication, treatment should be stopped immediately and the fluid deficiency should be corrected.

items.t: Mild hypercalciuria or history of stones: monitor urinary calcium. Impaired renal function: serum calcium and phosphate. High dose or with vitamin D: serum calcium and renal function.

src.q: monitoring of calcium excretion in the urine is required.
In these patients serum calcium levels should be followed and renal function should be monitored.

items.t: Reduce the dose or stop if urinary calcium is raised.

src.q: If necessary, the calcium dose should be reduced or therapy should be discontinued.

administration.note: No UK SmPC exists for the clinic syrup. The UK calcium effervescent tablet is dissolved in water, which does not apply to the syrup. Use the clinic label.

items.t: Do not take within 2 hours of spinach, rhubarb or whole cereals. Keep a gap from tetracycline antibiotics.

src.q: The patient should not take calcium products within two hours of eating foods high in oxalic acid and phytic acid.

items.t: If prone to kidney stones, drink plenty of fluids.

src.q: An increased fluid intake is recommended for patients prone to formation of calculi in the urinary tract.
